branch_provenance.syndrome: Subacute Unilateral Vision Loss with Conjunctival and Neurological Alarm Signs

state.case_summary:
A woman in her late 50s was hospitalized in March 2020 for severe bilateral pneumonia. She had recent close contact with a fatal case. No relevant medical history was reported. On day 2 post-admission, she developed blurred vision and redness in her right eye and temporary (8-day) pain when mobilizing the globe.

Best-corrected visual acuity was +2 logMAR (hand movement) OD and 0 logMAR OS. The right eye had:- Relative afferent pupil defect- Central scotoma- Impaired color and contrast vision- Central nongranulomatous retrodescemetic precipitates - Mild anterior chamber inflammation- Noticeable pupillary edema- 2 peripapillary hemorrhages- Mild vitreous inflammation- Retinal vessel narrowing in the inferior retinaContralateral eye examinations were normal. No other neurological symptoms were observed.

- Laboratory Tests:  * Normal complete blood cell counts  * Normal serum angiotensin-converting enzyme levels  * Normal human leukocyte antigen B51/B27 typing  * Negative results for syphilis, HIV, Toxoplasma gondii, and Borrelia serologies  * Negative IgM and very weakly positive IgG for VZV, HSV, EBV, and CMV  * Positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2  * Negative CSF SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR- Imaging Studies:  * Cranial MRI with fine optic nerve cuts (normal results)  * Fluorescein Angiography (Day 30):    Image Title: Optic disc neuritis    Image Description: Mild leakage associated with inferior peripapillary hemorrhage        Image Title: Retinal vasculitis    Image Description: Fluorescein leakage from retinal venules inferotemporal to the macula    * Papillary OCT (Days 30 & 48):    Image Description: Progression from discrete right papillary edema to severe optic nerve atrophy

alarm_features: recent close contact with a fatal case
excluded_candidates: Infectious posterior uveitis: unlikely given the absence of other systemic symptoms
Inflammatory optic neuritis: possible, but the presence of retinal vasculitis and peripapillary hemorrhage suggests a more complex pathology
Neoplastic process: unlikely given the acute presentation and the absence of other systemic symptoms
